title: Ancillary and Optional Services Billing: Applying Payments and Crediting Charges
content:
§1 Payments. Under Ancillary and Optional Services Billing a payment names the charge it pays and is applied only up to its open balance; a transfer from the resident's trust account is posted only on the per-bill authorization recorded with the trust account.

§2 Credits. A charge billed for an item the payer covers, bundled under consolidated billing, related to a hospice terminal illness, never requested, or priced wrongly is credited in full or for the excess, naming the charge. A charge is credited once per reason.

§3 Disputes. A resident may dispute a charge within the dispute window days after the statement date, and a dispute is resolved within the dispute resolution business days; a dispute decided for the resident is credited as dispute upheld.

The statement date is day 4 of the month, on which the prior month's charges are billed; the dispute window is 60 calendar days after the statement date, and the dispute resolution period is 10 business days.

## The open balance of a charge

The open balance of a charge, as of the posting date, is the amount of that charge less the payments and credits that name it. The amount applied from a payment is the lesser of the payment amount and that open balance. Payments are accepted by check, ACH, card or trust transfer.

| Hypothetical charge | Earlier entries naming it | Payment received | Open balance | Amount applied |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| USD 61.35 | Credit of USD 7.50 | USD 70.00 | USD 53.85 | USD 53.85 |
| USD 61.35 | Credit of USD 7.50 | USD 20.00 | USD 53.85 | USD 20.00 |

## Credit reasons

| Reason recorded with the credit | The charge was billed for |
|---|---|
| Payer covered item | An item the payer covers |
| Consolidated billing item | An item bundled under consolidated billing |
| Hospice related item | An item related to a hospice terminal illness |
| Not requested | An item never requested |
| Price error | An item priced wrongly |
| Dispute upheld | A charge whose dispute was decided for the resident |

A hypothetical haircut charged at USD 25.00 against a schedule price of USD 22.00 is priced wrongly by USD 3.00, the excess. The once-per-reason limit is read from the company's ledger, by the charge and the reason the credit names: a second credit for the same charge and the same reason is not posted.

## Trust transfers

A payment by transfer from the resident's trust account is posted only on the per-bill authorization recorded with the trust account. A trust transfer with no such authorization on record for that bill is not posted.
